title: False-positive rapid diagnostic test for malaria in new world cutaneous leishmaniasis: a tale of two travelers
case_text: A 47-year-old man who was a traveling companion of the patient described above presented with a total of 10 lesions on bilateral upper (Figure 2) and lower extremities and flank, all >1 cm with the largest measuring 5 cm. Tissue samples were sent to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Atlanta, GA, USA, for confirmation of diagnosis. Samples from our two patients were positive for Leishmaniasis by immunohistochemistry and histopathologic evidence of amastigotes in both cases. Both received an initial 3-day course of liposomal amphotericin B (Ambisome ) followed by miltefosine (Impavido ). They were treated with a total 28-day course of miltefosine with eventual resolution of lesions. As part of their clinical workup to rule out malaria, a rapid malaria antigen testing for P falciparum was obtained and reported positive in both patients (BinaxNOW malaria, Abbott Laboratories, Elk Grove Village, IL, USA). However, both a qualitative RT-PCR for P falciparum in blood (ARUP Laboratories, Salt Lake City, UT, USA) and repeated thick-and-thin smear direct microscopy were negative in both patients.

   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:

     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Leishmaniasis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: cutaneous leishmaniasis with false-positive rapid malaria test
